parties: DPSC Limited; India Power Corporation Limited (IPCL); Committee of Creditors (CoC)
headline: DPSC Limited: Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process – 4th CoC Meeting of India Power Corporation Limited
sum: DPSC Limited has disclosed the post-facto intimation of the 4th Committee of Creditors meeting under the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) for India Power Corporation Limited (IPCL), signalling continuation of structured creditor deliberations under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code.
implication: The progression to a fourth CoC meeting indicates a complex, multi-stage resolution negotiation; counsel should monitor the resolution plan status, especially treatment of secured vs. unsecured creditors and any proposed haircuts, as these shape recovery scenarios and precedent for similar power-sector insolvencies.
detail: DPSC Limited (a listed entity) has filed a post-facto intimation with the NSE regarding the 4th meeting of the Committee of Creditors convened under CIRP for India Power Corporation Limited (IPCL). The disclosure is made under Regulation 30 of the SEBI LODR, 2015, as required when a listed company or its related party undergoes material corporate governance events. The successive CoC meetings suggest the debtor is in an advanced or contested phase of resolution negotiations; typical CIRP timelines under IBC §12 allow 180 days (extendable by 90 days) for a resolution plan to be approved and submitted to the tribunal.

framework.note: central - governs CIRP duration (180 days + max 90-day extension), CoC formation, and resolution plan approval threshold (66% by value of financial debt)
central - defines Committee of Creditors composition, voting rights, and decision-making quorum (≥50% by value of financial debt)
central - sets out resolution plan evaluation criteria, condition precedents, and approval requirements
central - mandates immediate disclosure by listed entities of material corporate governance events; CIRP proceedings are considered material

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI) Regulations, 2016 (Rules & Regulations)
framework.note: amended - governs insolvency professional conduct, CoC meetings, and reporting; last substantially amended 2024
central - procedural framework for CIRP petitions, tribunal jurisdiction, and adjudication of disputes between CoC and resolution professional
applicable - sets tariff and regulatory obligations for power utilities; relevant if IPCL holds power generation/distribution licenses subject to regulator approval in resolution
amended - requires post-facto disclosure within one day for material information not disclosed during the meeting; this intimation is post-facto, triggering this requirement

conditions: Continuation of CoC deliberations and resolution plan formulation under IBC § 31
Achievement of 66% by value of financial debt CoC approval (voting threshold)
Compliance with NCLT filing and tribunal approval
Adherence to CIRP statutory timeline (180-day base + up to 90-day extension)
approvals: NCLT approval of resolution plan (mandatory before implementation)
CoC majority vote (66% by value of financial debt)
Sector regulator approval if IPCL holds power distribution or generation licenses (Electricity Act, 2003)

triggers.note: CIRP timeline commencement and statutory duration constraints; resolution plan must be approved within 180 days or filed for tribunal extension
Mandatory disclosure by DPSC Limited (as related/connected party or debtor's related entity) of CoC proceedings and material meetings
CoC quorum, voting protocol, and resolution professional reporting; fourth meeting suggests complex or disputed resolution negotiations
If IPCL is a power utility, any resolution plan change of control or asset sale may require sector regulator (CERC/SERC) clearance
